title: Referencing styles
examples: What is the main difference between APA and MLA?
When do I use an in-text citation versus a full reference?
Which style is best for a literature review?

explain.say: Today we look at different ways to cite sources properly.

items: APA: Focuses on date and source.
MLA: Focuses on author and page number.
Harvard: Author and date are key.

explain.say: The first subtopic is the American Psychological Association style, or APA.
Next we look at the Modern Language Association style, or MLA.
The third style we cover is Harvard referencing, which is another author-date system.
In-text citations are short mentions right where you use the idea.
The full reference list provides all details at the end of your paper.

faq.q: Do I always need a reference list if I cite in the text?
faq.a: Yes, you must always have a reference list. The in-text citation points to the full details in the list.
asks: What if I only cite in the text?

faq.q: If I use APA, do I use the same format for MLA?
faq.a: No, the formats are different. APA prioritizes the date, while MLA focuses on the page number.
asks: Can I mix APA and MLA?

faq.q: What is the difference between a citation and a reference?
faq.a: A citation is the short mention in the text. A reference is the full entry in the list at the end.
asks: What is the difference between citing and referencing?

faq.q: Which style should I use for a science report?
faq.a: APA style is most commonly used for social sciences and many scientific reports. Always check your assignment guidelines first.
asks: What style is best for biology?

faq.a: Harvard is an author-date system, but specific rules can vary by institution. Always confirm the required variation.
asks: Do I need a specific Harvard guide?

facts: APA style emphasizes the year of publication for source credibility.
MLA style typically uses the author and page number for location.
All styles require a consistent format for both in-text and reference list entries.
Harvard is an author-date system that requires author and date.

quiz.say: If you mention Smith's idea in your paragraph, what must you include immediately?
quiz.why: This format correctly uses the author and year for an in-text citation, which is standard for APA.

wrong.0: This lacks the required punctuation to separate the name and the year.
wrong.2: This misses the necessary punctuation and flow for a parenthetical citation.
wrong.3: This mixes page location with the year, which is not the standard format.

quiz.say: Which style focuses heavily on the page number in the citation?
quiz.why: MLA style is known for its emphasis on the author and the specific page number where the quote appears.

wrong.0: Harvard is an author-date system, making the year more prominent than the page number.
wrong.1: While both use authors, MLA is the style that most strongly features the page number in its core citation structure.
wrong.3: APA prioritizes the date of publication over the specific page number in the main citation.

quiz.say: When creating the final list of sources, what is the general rule?
quiz.why: The full list of sources, containing all necessary details, belongs in the reference list, not in the text.

wrong.0: In-text citations are only short pointers used within the body of your writing.
wrong.1: While similar, 'Bibliography' is a general term; the specific list required is usually called a Reference List.
wrong.2: Footnotes are used for supplementary notes, not for the main listing of sources.
